newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs firm late to close mixed, pork bellies up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs firm late to close mixed, pork bellies up.

text.p: CME lean hog futures firmed late on higher-than-expected cash hog prices to close mixed while pork belly futures again closed moderately higher ahead of the weekly CME out-of-town report, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.350 cent per lb higher to 0.450 lower with June off 0.100 at 80.775 cents and July up most at 82.150 cents. Pork bellies finished mostly 0.800 cent per lb higher to unchanged with July up most at 89.300 cents.
Firmer-than-expected cash pork prices at noon and ideas of steady to higher cash hog prices Wednesday prompted renewed support in hog futures late, traders said.
USDA in its central carlot report quoted hams steady to $1.00 higher and loins firm. Bellies and trimmings sold fully steady.

Futures eased early on profit taking after three days of gains, the premium futures hold to cash hog prices and concern cash pork values have been weak despite recent light slaughter. The latest CME lean hog index fell $1.19 to $78.31 per cwt while June hog futures ended Monday at 80.875 cents, they said.

However, wholesale pork prices were steady to firmer at noon and hog runs remained light which sparked ideas of stronger cash hog prices Wednesday. Renwed commercial buying took prices up for net gains before profit taking pared levels at the closing bell.

R.J. O'Brien and Rand Financials bought July on the rally but Rand sold at the close, traders said. Rand also bought August against selling by Lind-Waldock. In hog options, LFG bought October 76 calls and Iowa Grain sold July 84 calls, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures swung widely during the day after posting an initial sharp gain on buy stops. Profit taking and some selling prompted by recent weakness in cash bellies thinned demand at times but the market again rallied ahead of the CME out-of-town report, traders said.
Expectations were for another out-movement of between 250,000 to 500,000 lbs last week. After the close, CME reported a net out-movement last week of 137,000 lbs.
Short covering was evident in the belly pit much of the day and again late, especially when hog futures rallied, they said.
Refco notably bought late after selling early. LFG and R.J. O'Brien also bought during the day to offset selling by Rand Financials and Lind-Waldock, pit sources added.
